title: India's 300th T20I Brings a First: 200 Outright Wins in the Format
excerpt: Saturday's four-wicket win over New Zealand in Christchurch was India's 300th men's T20I and their 200th outright win — a landmark reached in a format they first played, almost as an experiment, in December 2006.
body:
• India played their 300th men's T20 international on Saturday in Christchurch, becoming only the second team after Pakistan (304) to reach the mark.
  • The four-wicket win over New Zealand was also India's 200th outright T20I win — the first team to reach that figure, alongside five Super Over wins and one bowl-out win.
  • India have now won their 50th, 100th, 150th, 250th and 300th T20Is; the 200th, in 2019-era scheduling, was the one milestone match they lost, according to ESPNcricinfo's stats account.
  • The milestone match doubled as a record chase: 68 runs in the last five overs and a record 69-run seventh-wicket stand, detailed in our match report.

India's second T20I against New Zealand at Hagley Oval on Saturday carried a weight the scoreline alone does not show. It was India's 300th men's Twenty20 international — only Pakistan, with 304, have played more — and the four-wicket win made India the first team to register 200 outright wins in the format, according to ESPNcricinfo's statistical account of the match.

From Experiment to Empire

India's T20I journey began on December 1, 2006, in Johannesburg, where a side led by Virender Sehwag beat South Africa by six wickets, with Dinesh Karthik named Player of the Match, as LatestLY's milestone report recounts. India treated the format cautiously at first — several senior players skipped the inaugural World Cup — and then won that 2007 tournament under MS Dhoni, a result that reshaped Indian cricket's economics and produced the IPL a year later.

The silverware since tells the arc: World Cup titles in 2007, 2024 and 2026, and a win record no other side matches. Pakistan have played four more T20Is than India but have registered substantially fewer victories; New Zealand sit third on the appearances list, well behind the two Asian sides.

A Milestone Match That Refused to Be Ceremonial

Landmark fixtures often pass quietly. This one did not. Chasing 181 after Glenn Phillips (70) and Bevon Jacobs (58) lifted New Zealand to 180 for 5, India collapsed to 112 for 6 against Mitchell Santner's 4 for 21 — at one point ESPNcricinfo's Forecaster put India's win probability at 5.21 percent. Tilak Varma's unbeaten 51 off 26 balls and his unbroken 69-run stand with Nitish Kumar Reddy, India's highest for the seventh wicket in T20Is, closed the chase with a ball to spare.

The closing burst set format records of its own: the 68 runs India scored in the last five overs are the most they have successfully chased in that phase of a T20I, passing the 60 against Pakistan at the MCG in the 2022 World Cup, and the 111 runs scored after the fall of the fifth wicket are India's most in a successful chase.

What 300 Matches Actually Shows

The number is partly a scheduling artefact — India play more bilateral T20 cricket than most — but the win column is not. Two hundred outright wins, plus five Super Over wins and a bowl-out win, across three distinct eras of players, with the current side winning a milestone match on the back of two batters aged in their early twenties, points to depth as the through-line. India's 50th, 100th, 150th and 250th T20Is were also wins; only the 200th was lost.

The Christchurch match also handed debuts to teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and pacer Prince Yadav — a reminder that even at match 300, the pipeline the milestone celebrates is still producing its next cohort.

What Comes Next

India lead the five-match series 2-0, with the third T20I in Wellington on October 27. Pakistan's 304-match mark is within reach this season; the wins record, already India's alone, is the one that will take other sides years to chase.
